title: Module Correlation, Health and Readiness Signal
description: What a runtime module reports about itself: the correlation identity that ties it to the workflow, whether it is alive, whether each of its capabilities is actually ready, and the closed set of labels its SLI may be tagged with. Liveness is defined so that it cannot depend on an external provider, and the label set is closed so that user content cannot become a metric dimension.

trace_id.x-source: DECLARED INFERENCE, previously UNSOURCED. Decision Register 5.2 names CTR-OBS-001 "Correlation/health/readiness" and OB-001 requires one trace to follow a workflow across retry, worker and adapter. Neither names a trace_id FIELD. Independent review found this rule shipped with no source while its four siblings were sourced, which falsified this package's claim that no rule lacks one.

correlation.x-source: Decision Register 5.2 CTR-OBS-001 requires 'propagation'; OB-001 requires ONE trace to follow a workflow across retry, worker and adapter; OBS-004 requires the browser, API, outbox, worker and provider spans to join up. The field names are Workstream 3.1 (`correlation_id`, `request_id`, `causation_id`) and 3.3 (`job_id`). `correlation_id` is the only required one because OB-001 makes it the identity that must survive a retry.

module.x-source: OB-003 aggregates health per MODULE and OBS-002 requires the module on every structured record. The `module_key` shape is CTR-MOD-001's, so a health signal and a module manifest name the same module; the pair module key plus implementation version is the Workstream 3.2 `producer`.

environment.x-source: OBS-002 requires the environment on every structured record. The four values are exactly the four rows of the Environment Model in the Meta/Security/Ops workstream Track INF: Local, Preview, Staging, Production.

liveness.x-source: OB-003 states the rule directly: liveness must NOT be tied to an external provider. It is a `const false` rather than a boolean because a liveness probe that admits a provider dependency is not a liveness probe -- a provider outage would restart every healthy module. This is the one place the contract can enforce the rule rather than describe it.

allOf.x-rule: MR-004 makes activation deny-by-default. MR-004 does NOT mention a reason; requiring one is a DECLARED INFERENCE from MR-006, which requires support to see the last error without seeing a secret. CTR-MOD-001 records the same correction, and OB-003 requires readiness to reflect the real capability: a capability reported as not ready without saying why is not actionable by the module owner OB-002 routes the alert to.

readiness.x-source: Decision Register 5.2 CTR-OBS-001 requires 'readiness'; OB-003 requires readiness to reflect the REAL capability and MR-004 produces a 'readiness result per capability/scope', which is why readiness is reported per capability rather than as one flag. `reason_key` is a stable key rather than free text because CM-004 and CTR-ERR-001 establish stable keys for anything a person reads and OBS-001 forbids full content on this path; key-not-prose is a DECLARED INFERENCE from CM-004 and CTR-ERR-001. `capability_key` matches CTR-MOD-001's.

status.x-source: DECLARED INFERENCE. The cited alert row reads "degraded provider, queue delay, one format unavailable" and draws no distinction between a degraded and an unavailable dependency; `healthy` appears in no source at all. The three values are this contract's own terms, inferred from that row plus OB-003 readiness. Independent review found the earlier citation claimed a distinction the source does not make.

dependencies.x-source: OB-003 aggregates 'module/provider status'. The `kind` split exists because the same task forbids an external provider from affecting liveness while allowing it to affect readiness, so the two must be distinguishable in the signal itself. The three status values are a DECLARED INFERENCE from the SEV-2 example in the Meta/Security/Ops alert table, which distinguishes a degraded provider from an unavailable one; no source enumerates them.

environment.x-source: Track INF deployment environments, the same four values this schema already closes for the envelope's own `environment` property 30 lines above. A label whose safe vocabulary the contract itself enumerates has no reason to be open free text: an open pattern here accepted a workspace id as an environment label, which is unbounded cardinality on a metric dimension OB-006 requires bounded. Raised by A6 in SRE co-owner review.

outcome.x-source: OB-006 bounded cardinality. LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY. A6 proposed closing this to CTR-AUD-001's `succeeded`/`failed`/`denied` in co-owner review; that set is the wrong one for this label. AUD's `outcome` is the result of an ACTOR'S ACTION; this label is the result of a health probe, and the contract's own fixtures use `success`, `down` and `provider_unavailable`. Reusing AUD's words rejects this contract's own valid documents. Closing this label needs an SLI outcome vocabulary, and no source states one -- the same position `error_code` is in. Recorded for the metric dictionary rather than invented here.

sli_tags.x-source: Decision Register 5.2 CTR-OBS-001 requires 'SLI tags' and 'bounded cardinality'; OB-006 requires that no user content, token or page name appears in a metric label and that cardinality is bounded. The label NAME set is therefore closed by additionalProperties false, which is what makes `page_name` -- OB-006's own example -- rejected rather than merely discouraged. `workspace_id` is deliberately absent: OBS-001 requires a workspace to be LINKABLE, and the correlation block and the structured log carry that, whereas a per-workspace metric label is exactly the unbounded dimension OB-006 forbids. `module_key` and `environment` are required because OBS-002 requires both on every structured record.
sli_tags.x-cardinality-limitation: This closes the set of label NAMES. It does not bound the set of label VALUES, and OB-006's requirement is about cardinality, which is a property of the value space. No source states a numeric budget and none is invented here. See examples/accepted-gap-unbounded-error-code-label.json and untestable_by_schema.

redaction.x-source: OBS-001 requires trace, job, workspace, module and error to stay linkable WITHOUT carrying a secret or full content; OBS-002 requires PII redaction tests to pass on the structured logging path; OB-002 requires PII to be redacted before an alert is routed.

allOf.x-rule: OB-003 'readiness reflects the real capability' with MR-004 deny-by-default: a module cannot report itself ready while listing a capability that is not. Without this, the aggregate flag and the capability list are two descriptions of one state that can disagree in silence.

OB-003 health aggregation with MR-004 deny-by-default: a module that is not alive cannot be ready. The converse is deliberately NOT stated -- a live module may be unready, which is precisely the case OB-003 protects when an external provider is unavailable.

x-catalog-note: Decision Register 5.2 lists this contract's freeze artifacts as "propagation, SLI tags, bounded cardinality". The word "readiness" appears in the row's NAME column, not among its required artifacts; an earlier annotation cited it as though it were an artifact requirement. Right row, wrong column.
